aka: Priory Church of St. Anthony, Lenton

stories.text: Henry II gave Lenton Priory an eight-day fair for St Martin's Day, which Henry III lengthened to twelve, with tolls paid to the monks for every booth. The fair outlived the priory: in 1584, when servants of Mary, Queen of Scots came, it was a horse fair, and by the 17th century it was known as a great fair for all sorts of horses. In the 19th century farmers and horse dealers still came.

William Peverel founded a priory of Cluniac monks at Lenton in about 1102–08, and richly endowed it. In February 1538 its last prior, Nicholas Heath, and many of his monks were thrown into prison, accused of high treason. The prior, eight monks and four Lenton labourers were executed, in Nottingham and in front of the priory, and the priory was dissolved that year. Little is left: the Priory Church of St Anthony is thought to keep part of its hospital chapel.

67476.sum: The Priory Church of St Anthony, Lenton, also known as The Priory, is a parish church in the Church of England in Lenton, Nottingham.

stories.text: Nottingham Victoria, the Great Central and Great Northern railways' station, opened on 24 May 1900 and closed on 4 September 1967. It was demolished except for its clock tower, which still stands at the entrance of the Victoria Centre built on the site.

75086.sum: Nottingham Victoria station: a takeaway. The building was built in 1899, according to OpenStreetMap. It is Grade II listed as Victoria Centre Clock Tower and was designed by Albert Edward Lambert.

stories.text: Gedling's railway station closed on 4 April 1960, though coal trains ran to the colliery for decades more. Its building is now a youth centre, and there are plans to reopen the line or make it a cycleway.

260511.sum: Gedling and Carlton railway station was a former railway station built to serve the villages of Gedling and Carlton in Nottinghamshire.

stories.text: Until the Inclosure Act of 1845 the area was open Clay Fields. The Act let the town take 1,068 acres for housing, and by 1880 the streets of terraced houses called New Town were complete. The terraces north of Victoria Park are listed, as a once common kind of house now mostly lost to bombs and clearance.

298577.sum: 1 to 30, the Promenade is a terrace of houses on Promenade. The building dates from about 1860, according to OpenStreetMap. It is Grade II listed.
